svg.title: Questions on kubernetes: Graphicle 0.1.8 against 0.1.7. Time per question (Median seconds per call): 22 questions, 16 cores: Graphicle 0.1.7 2.99 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 1.34 s; 22 questions, 4 cores: Graphicle 0.1.7 3.89 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 1.38 s; 22 questions, 4 cores, cold: Graphicle 0.1.7 4.55 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 1.90 s; 8 lookups, 16 cores: Graphicle 0.1.7 2.52 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 0.96 s. Peak memory of a call (Median, 22 questions, 16 cores): Graphicle 0.1.7 3.5 GB, Graphicle 0.1.8 0.6 GB.
svg.desc: Questions on kubernetes: Graphicle 0.1.8 against 0.1.7. Time per question (Median seconds per call): 22 questions, 16 cores: Graphicle 0.1.7 2.99 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 1.34 s; 22 questions, 4 cores: Graphicle 0.1.7 3.89 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 1.38 s; 22 questions, 4 cores, cold: Graphicle 0.1.7 4.55 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 1.90 s; 8 lookups, 16 cores: Graphicle 0.1.7 2.52 s, Graphicle 0.1.8 0.96 s. Peak memory of a call (Median, 22 questions, 16 cores): Graphicle 0.1.7 3.5 GB, Graphicle 0.1.8 0.6 GB. graphicle context, each call a new process, as the prompt hook runs it. Shorter bars are better. Same packets: On the same store, both releases gave the same packet for every question, byte for byte. Our Linux server (Intel Xeon Platinum 8480C), 16 of its cores, or 4 for a laptop-like run; kubernetes at ca8a2a9e4, a shallow clone (30,315 files); the 22 questions of issue #8 and 8 lookups such as “Where is X defined?”; both releases on the same cores, interleaved; medians. Cold: the data folder and the program dropped from the file cache before each call. Rounds and method: github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md#our-own-run-on-kubernetes-017-and-018
